answer.rationale: Memory_91 only reports a short-term proxy metric (week-one engagement/first action) with no link to revenue, retention, or customer quality, making it the weakest evidence for sustainable qualified revenue. Memory_57 is the strongest because it explicitly ties an intervention to 'qualified revenue' and checks for retention harm, directly matching the objective. Memory_44 and memory_73 mention revenue-adjacent outcomes (pipeline quality, revenue lift) but lack long-term/sustainability evidence—memory_73 especially is risky since promotional pricing tends to attract price-sensitive, low-loyalty customers, and no retention or margin data is given. Memory_31 and memory_86 report only activation/completion/adoption improvements without any connection to downstream revenue or retention, so they offer indirect, weak support.
